SPACE CRAFT JOURNAL / HYBRID & ADAPTABLE WORK

Innovative coworking space design ideas to boost productivity.

Plan around the patterns, not the label. This Space Craft planning note looks at innovative coworking space design ideas to boost productivity through the choices that affect everyday use, the details worth testing and the questions to take into your project brief.

Space Craft editorialPlanning note · 4 min read
IN THIS NOTEUnderstand attendance over timeSupport the reason to be thereMake change easy to manageAsk people what gets in the wayBefore you decide
01 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Understand attendance over time

Look beyond average attendance to days when teams overlap, visitors arrive or projects bring people together. Shared seats need an operating plan as well as a furniture plan.

02 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Support the reason to be there

Decide which activities benefit from being together and which need concentration or privacy. Give those activities appropriate settings instead of making the whole office uniformly collaborative.

03 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Make change easy to manage

Movable furniture, shared storage and clear room-use conventions can help. Assign responsibility for reset and upkeep so flexibility does not become daily uncertainty.

04 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Ask people what gets in the way

Invite input on distractions, access, comfort and the settings people cannot currently find. A workplace brief should allow different experiences to be heard.

BEFORE YOU DECIDE

Take this into your brief.

  • Map peak and typical attendance separately.
  • Test a shared-seat day from arrival to departure.
  • Agree storage and reset conventions.

Write down one priority, one constraint and one question you still need to answer. Review them beside the plan or material sample before agreeing the next design decision.

KEEP EXPLORING

Another angle on your space.

Hybrid & adaptable work

Activity-based working is an operating model before it is a layout.

ABW is often sold as a furniture style. It is better understood as an agreement about how people choose where to work, supported by neighbourhoods, lockers, booking and a clear-desk habit, and tested on one floor first.

↗Hybrid & adaptable work

A hybrid office should not have a second class of participant.

When some people join from home and others from the room, the room decides who is heard. Cameras, audio, small call rooms, booking rules and shared tools can make every seat equal.
